climbing_route.label: East ridge / east side to the summit
climbing_route.class: mostly low Class 3 with occasional short Class 4 moves
climbing_route.notes: From the rock/heather benches below Berdeen Peak's east side, climb directly over the 6,400–6,420 ft summit via the east ridge/east side. Easy-to-moderate terrain on steep, mossy rock — choose holds carefully, moss-covered rock is slick, especially wet. Loose blocks and exposed dirt/heather steps along the ridge crest are the main scramble-specific hazards; a helmet is worth carrying. North-facing terrain can hold lingering snow well into midsummer.

climbing_route.label: Guidebook spur-ridge bypass (avoids the top)
climbing_route.notes: The guidebook line contours around the summit on a spur ridge to avoid the top entirely, rather than climbing over it.

climbing_route.label: Quien Sabe Glacier to the Sahale-Boston col, then the Boston Glacier
climbing_route.notes: From high camp, an alpine start; rope up the Quien Sabe Glacier to the Sahale-Boston col (~8,200 ft), then cross the head of the Boston Glacier past the bergschrund to the base of the southeast-side ledges. Crevasse danger on the Quien Sabe/Boston Glacier crossing, worsening through the season as the bergschrund opens.

climbing_route.label: Southeast-side ledges
climbing_route.notes: Ascend unroped via loose, sandy ledges on the east/southeast face — unroped specifically to minimize rockfall exposure to parties below. Loose rock on the ledges; typical North Cascades afternoon rockfall and softening, so an alpine start is standard.

climbing_route.label: Crux below the summit ridge, then the summit scramble
climbing_route.notes: A crux move just below the summit ridge (loose rock here too), then a short scramble to the top.

climbing_route.label: Steep grassy/heather slopes into the south/southeast gullies
climbing_route.notes: Leave the PCT about a half-mile short of Chikamin Pass, near the ~5,200 ft pack camp, and climb steep grassy/heather slopes into the gully systems on the south/southeast face. Do not continue on to Chikamin Pass itself before cutting uphill — that puts you in the middle of the Four Brothers, a band of cliffy towers that force technical terrain. From the Glacier Lake side the same gullies are gained above the lake, with brooks, waterfalls, tarns, heather benches, sandstone slabs and blocky breccia low down.

climbing_route.label: Upper gully system to Chikamin Ridge
climbing_route.notes: Above treeline the gully system is loose scree and dirt-and-heather slots in its upper sections; some exposure near the final ridge crest as you gain Chikamin Ridge.

climbing_route.label: Chimney/slot below the summit block
climbing_route.notes: A short, well-protected chimney/slot sits right below the summit block on some lines, before the summit horn.

climbing_route.label: Lower Chimney Glacier to the toe of the south peak
climbing_route.notes: From the bivy basin, rope up and cross the lower Chimney Glacier, working toward the toe of the south peak rather than the main-summit gully used by the East Face. Be ready to improvise around the moat at the base of the face, which gets worse later in the season.

climbing_route.label: Pitch 1 — grooves and cracks right of the Rappel Chimney
climbing_route.notes: Route-description sources place the start of Pitch 1 in grooves and cracks roughly 30-40 feet climber's-right of the obvious 'Rappel Chimney' feature on the west face, reached via a short glacier crossing and scramble from the basin. Published beta on this glacier-to-base connection is thinner than for the East Face line, so budget extra route-finding time.

climbing_route.label: Talus/scree gullies to the ~6,300 ft bench
climbing_route.notes: Above the basin, gain the ~6,300 ft bench via talus/scree gullies or the vegetated slopes just left of them. Early-season parties will find snow gullies here — ice axe/crampons recommended — that are faster than the loose summer scree.

climbing_route.label: Southwest face slabs and gullies
climbing_route.notes: From the bench, the standard finish is a scramble up slabs and gullies on the southwest face.

climbing_route.label: Crux section gaining the summit ridge
climbing_route.notes: The short section gaining the summit ridge is the route's crux — loose, exposed rock.

climbing_route.label: Summit traverse
climbing_route.notes: An easy ~100 ft rightward (west) traverse along the ridge leads to the summit.

climbing_route.label: Talus/scree to the ~7,500 ft col on the southeast ridge
climbing_route.notes: From the Bird Lakes basin, climb talus/scree southeast to a col (~7,500 ft) on Devore's southeast ridge, passing beneath a pair of distinctive rock towers locally called 'the Bottles.' Expect lingering snow in the basin and on the col approach well into July, sometimes requiring an ice axe/crampons on a short ~40-degree traverse; loose rock and occasional avalanche debris are the main hazards on this upper section.

climbing_route.label: West along the summit ridge / west flank
climbing_route.notes: From the col the route turns west along the summit ridge/west flank — ledges and shallow gullies of variable rock quality, some solid, some 'kitty-litter'-covered slab, with a route-finding crux threading the ledge systems below the summit block.

climbing_route.label: Gentle snow above Glacier Gap camp
climbing_route.notes: Summit day from the ~7,300 ft Glacier Gap high camp is roughly 5.25 mi with about 2,350 ft of gain and 835 ft of intermediate descent; it starts by climbing gentle snow above camp.

climbing_route.label: Volcanic scree onto the Gerdine and Cool glaciers
climbing_route.notes: Follow a climber's track on volcanic scree onto the Gerdine and Cool glaciers, end-running a crevasse or two.

climbing_route.label: Final steep pitch to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Rejoin the climber's trail for the final steep pitch to the summit.

climbing_route.label: Open ridge boot path to the West Peak false summit
climbing_route.notes: Beyond the official trail terminus near 5,600 ft the route leaves maintained tread for an open ridge boot path: about 0.8 mi and 1,000 ft more to the ~6,600-ft West Peak false summit. Snow lingers well into summer (reports note solid snow from ~4,300-4,500 ft), so carry an ice axe from around that elevation upward, and expect crampons or snowshoes to be useful in early/late season.

climbing_route.label: False summit bypass
climbing_route.notes: Do not push straight over the false summit's top — it is corniced and exposed; bypass it on the south or west slope.

climbing_route.label: Notch/col and the final ridge to the East summit
climbing_route.notes: Past the false summit the ridge drops roughly 300 ft into a notch/col, then climbs a final ~1,400 ft of mixed snow, rock, and short exposed steps to the true (East) summit at 6,892 ft.

climbing_route.label: Knife-edge crux near the top
climbing_route.notes: A narrow, moderately exposed knife-edge-ish section near the top is the crux of the scramble — keep the axe in hand and self-arrest-ready on the steep snow. No reliable water beyond the creek crossings in the first mile.
